subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow load-time repair that deletes only dead-end same-parent compaction siblings, or require write-side prevention before repairing persisted transcripts?
rationale: The remaining fix touches persisted session history and can remove existing JSONL entries, so automation should not decide that data-repair policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept narrow repair policy
options.body: Refresh the linked PR over current main and land the compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression coverage for current repair/cache behavior.

options.title: Require write-side prevention first
options.body: Pause the repair PR and implement retry idempotency or superseding at compaction write time before deciding how to migrate existing forked files.

options.title: Reject deletion-based repair
options.body: Keep recovery manual and replace the PR with diagnostics-only detection if deleting persisted entries is not acceptable.

recommendation.title: Accept narrow repair policy
recommendation.body: Refresh the linked PR over current main and land the compaction-only dead-end deletion rule with regression coverage for current repair/cache behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a session-state policy call, and recent current-main history plus the previous review route point to steipete as the best available decision owner.
